title: Notable geography, locations, and navaids for Alenuihaha Channel crossing generally listed in order of location/appearance from start location on Big Island (Honokohau Harbor), north to Nishimura Bay, crossing the Alenuihaha to south Maui (Ahihi Bay), then back across Alenuihaha to Honokohau Harbor.

places.name: Hawaiʻi Island (Big Island)
places.label: Hawaiʻi Island
places.notes: Hawaiʻi Island, also called the Big Island, is the largest and youngest island in the Hawaiian archipelago, home to active volcanoes.

places.name: Kohala (5,480')
places.label: Kohala
places.notes: Kohala, the oldest and extinct volcano on Hawaiʻi Island

places.name: Waimea Valley (2,670')
places.label: Waimea Saddle
places.notes: Waimea Valley, situated in the uplands of the Kohala region on Hawaiʻi Island, is a windy area due to trade winds funneled through the valley between Kohala and Mauna Kea. These strong winds amplify conditions in the ʻAlenuihāhā Channel.

places.name: Mauna Kea (13,803′)
places.label: Mauna Kea
places.notes: Tallest peak in Hawaiʻi; significant for cultural importance and astronomical observatories.

places.name: Humuʻula Saddle (6,632')
places.label: Humuʻula Saddle
places.notes: The Humuʻula Saddle, located between Mauna Kea and Mauna Loa on Hawaiʻi Island, is a high-altitude valley known for its strong trade winds and dramatic weather. These winds, funneled through the Saddle, contribute to the powerful gusts and challenging conditions in the ʻAlenuihāhā Channel.

places.name: Mauna Loa (13,679′)
places.label: Mauna Loa
places.notes: World's largest active volcano; dominates the landscape of Hawaiʻi Island.

places.notes: Home port for S/V Solstice and departure for expedition. A well-equipped marina on Hawaiʻi Island's west coast, offering safe anchorage and amenities.

places.label: Off Pūhili Point

places.label: Kikaua Point

places.name: Mahewalu Point
places.label: Mahewalu Point

places.name: Fish Aggregating Device (FAD) "OT Waikōloa, Hawaiʻi"
places.label: FAD OT
places.meaning: Waters Pulling Far" or "Duck Water", name of wind
places.notes: Fish Aggregating Devices (FAD) located near Waikōloa; attracts pelagic fish species, beneficial for fishing activities. Fish in the north and west Pacific gather under floating objects, and FADs, ranging from advanced buoys with tracking equipment to simple logs, facilitate this. Hawaiian FADs, established by the state, are yellow with a 6-foot base, a 5-foot steel pole with a quick-flashing yellow light, and 12-inch white letters. Since FADs can break loose or lose their lighting, mariners are advised to use caution near them.

routes.label: ʻAlenuihāhā expedition route (option)
routes.note: One option: Honokōhau north to the base camps, then from Nishimura Bay across the channel and back. The turnaround is on the channel's throat line (ʻUpolu Point across to Kīpahulu, its narrowest crossing), 1 nm short of Maui's coast. The route ends at Nishimura; the way home to Honokōhau retraces legs 1 and 2. Straight legs; not a plan, and not for navigation.
